annotation.kind: project-corrected backward-error half of Lemma 4.2 with the proof-required iterate comparison made explicit

assumptions: A is a nonsingular real n by n matrix with n > 0, and b is a nonzero real vector.
The task represents one fixed iteration i of generic iterative refinement; it does not require MOD-GMRES.
The computed residual and update satisfy the exact operation equations and Euclidean error bounds (4.1)-(4.2).
The computed correction satisfies the residual bound (4.14).
epsilonR, epsilonU, w_i, and omega_i are nonnegative; the epsilonR and epsilonU families tend to zero.
Project correction: the first-order comparison ||xHat_i||_2 lesssim ||xHat_(i+1)||_2 used after equation (4.18) is an explicit theorem hypothesis.
The project represents lesssim by an eventual inequality with an O(scale^2) remainder, where scale tends to zero.
The real-valued normwise operation model makes no claim about overflow, underflow, NaNs, infinities, or subnormals.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p16_t2_corrected_restarted_residual_recurrence {n : Nat} {iota : Type*} {l : Filter iota} [l.NeBot] (A : P16Matrix n) (b : P16Vector n) (iteration : Nat) (scale : iota -> Real) (hscale : Tendsto scale l (nhds 0)) (hn : 0 < n) (hA : p16IsNonsingular A) (hb : b != 0) (step : P16Lemma42BackwardStep l scale A b iteration) (hiterate : p16FirstOrderLeAt l scale (fun t => p16VecNorm (step.xHat t)) (fun t => p16VecNorm (step.xHatNext t))) : exact identity (4.18) for every family member /\ p16FirstOrderLeAt l scale nextResidual recurrenceEnvelope
formal_statement.plain_language: For one computed generic iterative-refinement step, explicitly assume the first-order current-to-next iterate norm comparison used by the published proof. Then equation (4.18) holds exactly and the next residual satisfies Lemma 4.2's recurrence up to an O(scale^2) remainder.

informal_proof: Derive (4.18) from the residual and update equations. Rewrite the next residual as (rHat-A*correction)-deltaR-A*deltaX, apply Euclidean triangle and Frobenius matrix-action bounds, and substitute (4.1), (4.2), and (4.14). Use the explicit project-correction hypothesis to replace ||xHat_i||_2 by ||xHat_(i+1)||_2 plus an O(scale^2) remainder. Since epsilonR tends to zero and is nonnegative, it is eventually at most one, so the hidden product remains O(scale^2). Collect the exact w_i and epsilonR+epsilonU+omega_i coefficients.
informal_statement: A project-corrected version of Lemma 4.2's backward-error clause: under the iterate-norm comparison used by the published proof, exact residual composition (4.18) and first-order recurrence (4.15) hold.

tier_rationale: The L proof directly combines NumStability.frobNorm_nonneg, vecNorm2_nonneg, vecNorm2_add_le, vecNorm2_neg, and vecNorm2_matMulVec_le_frobNorm_mul with the paper-specific computed-step equations.
